scope: Official public-source review for a Japan MVP path integrating RockstarOS with existing satellite connectivity; no provider contact, contract, test booking, or real connection was performed.

recommendation.mvp: Integrate with an existing mobile network operator direct-to-cell service and its approved handset/app path; keep the carrier responsible for connectivity contracting and billing unless reseller rights and APIs are explicitly contracted.
recommendation.ownConstellation: Keep as a separately funded and regulated long-term feasibility study; do not make it a prerequisite for the first product.
recommendation.hardware: Treat handset direct-to-cell and an external satellite terminal as separate connection adapters. An eSIM alone does not provide the RF front-end, antenna, network authorization, or service entitlement.

findings.topic: KDDI au Starlink Direct consumer eligibility
confirmed: UQ/povo/other-carrier users may apply for the dedicated plan
public consumer plan and its displayed prices are not wholesale/resale terms
selected app data is supported and voice calling is not supported per current page

findings.topic: KDDI supported device and developer path
confirmed: Android 16+ and iOS 26+ are listed for supported-app development
eligible SIM/eSIM plan and supported handset are required
Android app manifest declaration and satellite-aware behavior are documented
app listing is application-based and may require a separate agreement/NDA
published listing criteria include six months since app release
mock tests cover latency/bandwidth/interruption but do not reproduce satellite-specific RF
Pixel 10 is listed as a mock-test handset
notProven: Pixel 10 GL066 field acceptance for Rockstar
real satellite RF/field behavior for Rockstar

confirmed: Google Pixel 10 family appears in the public supported-device list as of research date
notProven: exact unlocked/carrier SKU GL066 entitlement and field acceptance
the complete RockstarOS software stack on this handset

confirmed: apps do not use constrained satellite networks by default
application manifest opt-in PROPERTY_SATELLITE_DATA_OPTIMIZED is required
apps should adapt to lower throughput, higher latency, bursts, queueing, and data limits
findings.implementationDecision: Do not enable manifest opt-in until low-bandwidth flows, queue/retry semantics, status indication, size limits, and test coverage are implemented.

confirmed: filing requirements depend on coordination category and frequency/service rules
filings contain orbital/network and antenna/interference parameters
complete submission is made through the ITU system by an administration
notProven: Japan-specific authorization pathway for a proposed Rockstar system
any spectrum, orbit, financing, manufacturing, launch, or operations feasibility

mvpSequence: Preserve local AI and already-accepted cloud jobs through total network loss.
Implement a connection-mode abstraction for terrestrial, constrained direct-to-cell, external terminal, and offline states.
Prioritize small status, cancellation, approval, and result-summary messages; queue and cap retries; exclude large model/artifact downloads on constrained links.
Implement and test Android low-bandwidth behavior before setting satellite manifest opt-in.
Verify exact handset SKU, Android version, service plan, account/billing ownership, and permitted application traffic with an operator.
Run mock-device/network tests, then contracted field tests. Do not treat mock results as satellite RF or Rockstar acceptance.

status.androidSatelliteManifestOptIn: not implemented; intentionally gated on low-bandwidth behavior and provider review
